target: the DOS witness thesis ("witness, don't trust self-report")
question: The whole thesis is that self-reports are untrustworthy, yet idea-scout, the superloop walks, and now this loop all EMIT self-reports (ledgers the fleet reads as truth) — is the witness layer itself witnessed, or has trust just moved up one level to "the ledger says so"?
why: If ledgers are trusted uncritically we have relabeled trust, not removed it. Challenges the load-bearing claim of internal/adjudicator + dos.

target: issue throughput as a progress metric
question: A fleet that both GENERATES issues (idea-scout, question-loop) and DRAINS them nightly — are we measuring real external progress, or just the velocity of an internal backlog cycling against itself?
why: ~200-issue nightly targets look like progress but may be a closed loop. What is the outside-the-system signal that fak is actually getting better? Nobody owns that number.

question: Every super loop folds debt "worst-first" — but who set the debt weights, and has anyone checked that worst-first ordering actually correlates with operator regret rather than just being self-consistent?
why: An unexamined ranking that everyone trusts is a single point of silent misallocation. The ordering may be optimal or merely stable; we don't know which.

target: the shared-trunk / lane discipline (no-branches, OFF_TRUNK guard)
question: Steelman the opposite: short-lived per-worker branches would eliminate trunk-collision risk entirely and let CI gate each change in isolation — so what does the trunk-only regime actually buy that outweighs the collisions the lane leases exist to prevent?
why: The lane/lease machinery is a large standing cost justified by trunk-only. If the premise is weaker than assumed, so is the machinery. See docs/branch-regime.md.

question: `make ci` green is required before every ship, but green witnesses "tests pass," not "the change is correct" — how many shipped-green commits were later reverted, and if that number is unknown, is green-first measuring quality or just measuring itself?
why: A gate whose false-negative rate is unmeasured is a gate we trust on faith. The revert-rate of green ships is a cheap, decisive number we apparently don't track.

target: the negation-operator research program (negframe L0-L4, activation patching, LoRA/SAE)
question: Over 50 open issues target negation/negframe with an L0-L4 stack down to activation patching and LoRA adapters, yet no external user is on record asking for negation handling — is a quarter of the recent backlog a real product need or a research aesthetic the fleet finds interesting to itself?
why: A large, self-consistent research cluster with no outside demand is the classic shape of a fleet optimizing for its own curiosity. Nobody owns the question of who asked for this.

target: the supervisor-agent seat keep-bit (#4477: babysitting counter must fall)
question: The seat's keep-bit is that the babysitting counter must fall or the seat is reverted, but the seat exists to absorb escalations before they reach a human — lowering that counter mechanically whether its judgment is good or bad; does the keep-bit measure decision quality or just the suppression of the very signal that would expose bad decisions?
why: If the success metric is mechanically moved by the intervention regardless of outcome, the keep-bit witnesses activity, not value — a self-confirming gate on a trust-critical seat.

target: the doctrine that health must stay a deterministic rung, no recognizer agent
question: The repo forbids an agent that RECOGNIZES fleet health, yet #4477 introduces an agent that consumes health witnesses and decides spawn/replace/replan/widen — what non-semantic line actually separates 'deciding on typed witnesses' from the forbidden 'recognizing,' or has the doctrine been redrawn to permit exactly what it prohibited?
why: A load-bearing prohibition that gets relabeled rather than defended is worse than no prohibition — it launders a forbidden pattern under a new name. See docs/notes/CONCEPT-SUPERVISOR-AGENT-SEAT-2026-07-13.md.

target: maintenance ownership of the 11 durable products vs research-seam attention
question: PRODUCT-STATUS counts 11 durable laptop products while the active backlog pours into model-internals research (negation operators, FP8 dequant, activation patching) — who is accountable for keeping the 11 shipped products from rotting while the fleet's attention flows to research seams?
why: Shipped surfaces decay silently when all new attention goes to greenfield research; no issue, scorecard, or seat appears to own regression of what already works.

target: the concept glossary as the fix for overloaded vocabulary
question: The glossary exists because 'cache' names a dozen things and gate/guard/witness blur together — but is that vocabulary sprawl itself the signal the system has accreted more concepts than it needs, and does a disambiguation scorecard let the fleet document the overload instead of asking whether the planes should be collapsed?
why: Disambiguating names treats the symptom; a dozen 'cache' planes may be genuine complexity or may be accidental accretion nobody is empowered to delete. The glossary makes the sprawl feel managed.

target: the 21 self-generated scorecards and their 0/100 rows
question: There are 21 scorecard docs each generated and graded by its own tool in the same repo, and 11 currently read 0/100 — when a card scores zero, is any real work actually driven by that number, or are failing scorecards just unowned dashboards with no consequence?
why: A gate with no owner and no consequence is theater; if a 0/100 sits unchanged, the scorecard measures nothing and its existence implies rigor that isn't there.

question: A product map can score a perfect honesty grade while describing products no one outside the repo uses — what would PRODUCT-STATUS look like if it also had to witness external adoption, and why is that column absent from a page that claims to answer whether you can use fak today?
why: Steelman the omission: an internal-honesty score is cheap to hold at 100 precisely because it never has to survive contact with a user. The absent adoption column is the load-bearing gap.
